sections.heading: Analysis cache
sections.text:
ssmdconvert report stores versioned JSON analysis snapshots and reusable
per-chapter preparation results in the user cache. Snapshots include the selected
source/chapter fingerprints, effective analysis options, generic preparation
results, SSMD mapping records, report data, and TXT projection metadata. Records
are checksummed and validated before reuse. The cache is local derived data, not
part of an SSMD document or book bundle.
sections.lower:

results, ssmd mapping records, report data, and txt projection metadata. records
are checksummed and validated before reuse. the cache is local derived data, not
part of an ssmd document or book bundle.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text:
If XDG_CACHE_HOME is set: $XDG_CACHE_HOME/ssmdconvert


Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Cache\ssmdconvert


Other platforms: ~/.cache/ssmdconvert



There is no cache-path CLI override. The cache uses separate chapters/,
analyses/, and index/ records beneath that root. A source index retains only a
bounded history of recent analysis IDs.

sections.heading: Reuse and freshness
sections.text:
Each report run recomputes SSMD-specific analysis and saves a source-level
snapshot. Compatible per-chapter preparation results are reused by default.
ssmdconvert report SOURCE --refresh bypasses cached per-chapter preparation and
reruns preparation for the selected sections before saving a fresh snapshot.
Re-running identical inputs may produce the same deterministic analysis ID.

Chapter preparation fingerprints include the linguistics policy, selected
provider/model, and their versions. Changing those values invalidates cached
preparation, while a compatible hit reuses results without running NLP over the
chapter.

source’s saved analyses and verifies only the current bytes of the affected
chapter. If those byt…

sections.heading: Removing or sharing cache data
sections.text:
To clear the cache, stop ssmdconvert and remove the ssmdconvert directory
under the location above. A later report recreates it. There is no command that
clears the cache automatically.

Cache files can contain source and prepared unit text used to render context, as
well as SSMD-derived data and fingerprints. Treat them as sensitive local data;
review a requested context --bug-report payload before sharing it. Deleting the
cache does not modify source SSMD, workspaces, or bundles.

sections.heading: SSMD analysis and speech workflows
sections.text:
SSMDConvert owns SSMD-specific source loading, chapter selection, language and
context semantics, source mapping, reporting, text projection, and safe
write-back. It uses the public ttsready Python API for source-neutral speech
preparation and QA.

Reports, context lookup, TXT projection, and speech workflows accept standalone
.ssmd or .ssmd.md files and canonical .ssmd-bundle directory or ZIP paths.
The bundle manifest determines whether the source contains a book or document.
Book chapter selection uses original one-based source numbers; a single document
has the section ID document-0001.

sections.heading: Python API and cache boundary
sections.text:
The root Python facade composes the same analysis, projection, report, and
speech materialization services as the CLI:

from ssmdconvert import (
    AnalysisOptions,
    TextProjectionOptions,
    analyze_ssmd,
    build_report,
    freeze_speech,
    lookup_change_context,
    project_text,
)

analysis = analyze_ssmd("notes.ssmd-bundle", options=AnalysisOptions(spacy="off"))
projection = project_text(analysis, options=TextProjectionOptions(max_paragraph_chars=1000))
report = build_report(analysis, projection=projection)
if analysis.preparation.changes:
    context = lookup_change_context(analysis, analysis.preparation.changes[0].id)
frozen = freeze_speech(analysis)  # returns rewritten section text; writes nothing

sections.heading: Local spaCy and progress
sections.text:
Bundle conversion, reports, TXT, and speech-preparation commands accept
--spacy off|auto|sm|md|lg|trf; the default is off. auto checks locally
installed models for each effective language and continues without hints if no
compatible model is available. Explicit tiers require their local model.
SSMDConvert never downloads spaCy or models.

Long-running commands accept --progress / --no-progress. Progress is
automatic only when stderr is a terminal. Rich UI or concise plain status output
is written to stderr; report, TXT, and JSON output remain on stdout. Python
callbacks are synchronous and provider-neutral.
sections.lower:

--spacy off|auto|sm|md|lg|trf; the default is off. auto checks locally
installed models for each effective language and continues without hints if no
compatible model is available. explicit tiers require their local model.
ssmdconvert never downloads spacy or models.

sections.heading: Context lookup
sections.text:
First create a report so the generic change ID is in the local analysis cache,
then request that ID for the same source:

ssmdconvert report novel.ssmd-bundle.zip
ssmdconvert context novel.ssmd-bundle.zip chg:v1:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
ssmdconvert context novel.ssmd-bundle.zip chg:v1:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef --paragraph --json




Context checks the current bytes of the affected chapter or document before
returning cached data. Editing that item makes its old analysis stale; rerun the
report with --refresh and use the new change ID. Unrelated chapter edits do not
invalidate another chapter’s context. Mixed-language paragraphs are shown as
whole paragraphs. Review --bug-report output for sensitive text before sharing.

sections.heading: TXT projection
sections.text:
ssmdconvert txt novel.ssmd-bundle.zip --chapters 2-8 -o prepared.txt
ssmdconvert txt notes.ssmd --no-include-titles




TXT is the generic prepared plain-text projection used by report previews and
statistics, not a substitute for SSMD: annotations are not included. Output goes
to stdout unless -o is given. Existing destinations require --force; the
input is never a valid output path.

sections.heading: Speech audit, annotate, and freeze
sections.text:
ssmdconvert speech audit notes.ssmd --json
ssmdconvert speech annotate notes.ssmd -o annotated.ssmd
ssmdconvert speech freeze novel.ssmd-bundle.zip --chapters 2-8 -o frozen.ssmd-bundle.zip




Audit is read-only and uses the same analysis pipeline and generic change IDs as
reporting. Annotation and freeze materialize eligible automatic decisions as
explicit SSMD substitutions. They validate source spans, reject unsafe or
overlapping edits, and preserve visible text. Existing authoritative
annotations are not duplicated; unresolved language or unsafe mappings prevent
write-back.

sections.heading: Bundle lifecycle
sections.text:
convert_bundle() detects the source kind, converts the input, and writes a
canonical directory workspace. inspect_bundle_source() inspects a source or
bundle. load_bundle() and validate_bundle() strictly verify supported
manifest content. load_bundle_workspace() reads current valid directory
content and reports dirty state; refresh_bundle_workspace() updates recorded
digests. pack_bundle() writes a canonical archive without changing the
workspace.

from ssmdconvert import (
    convert_bundle,
    inspect_bundle_source,
    load_bundle,
    pack_bundle,
    refresh_bundle_workspace,
    validate_bundle,
)

result = convert_bundle("novel.epub", output="novel.ssmd-bundle")
assert result.kind == "book"
loaded = load_bundle(result.output)
assert loaded.kind == result.kind

sections.heading: EPUB source conversion
sections.text:
EPUB is the book source format. Use the shared bundle commands to inspect the
navigation inventory and convert all or selected chapters:

ssmdconvert bundle inspect novel.epub --json
ssmdconvert bundle convert novel.epub --chapters 1 -o chapter-one.ssmd-bundle
ssmdconvert bundle convert novel.epub --chapters 1,3-5 -o selected.ssmd-bundle
ssmdconvert bundle convert novel.epub --chapters 2-20 -o selected.ssmd-bundle




Selectors use original one-based source chapter numbers. They refer to the
complete source inventory even when the output contains a subset. Selected
chapters remain in source order; duplicate numbers do not duplicate chapters.
Missing chapters, zero or negative numbers, reversed ranges, and malformed
tokens are rejected.

sections.heading: Book manifest format (implementation detail)
sections.text:
This page documents the existing book manifest carried inside a canonical
bundle. It is an implementation detail; users manage either source kind through
the common lifecycle described in Bundle workspaces.

The book manifest keeps its existing format identifier and schema version:

format:         ssmdconvert.book
schema_version: 1
ssmd_version:   0.9

array. Each chapter entry identifies the stable chapter ID, original source
number, relative SSMD path, title, navigation references, character count, and
SHA-256 digest. The array order is authoritative; directory filenames are not
used to infer reading order. Chapter documents remain independently valid SSMD
0.9.

sections.heading: Validation and workspace behavior
sections.text:
Strict loading and validation check the manifest format and versions, normalized
relative paths, duplicate IDs and members, UTF-8, SSMD validity, and source and
chapter digests. ZIP symlinks and unsafe paths are rejected. The loader applies
bounds to manifest size, chapter sizes, total referenced content, and archive
member count.

An editable directory can be loaded as a workspace when chapter text is valid
but its recorded digest is stale. The workspace reports dirty state and current
content without rewriting the manifest. bundle refresh is the explicit
operation to update digests and character counts. bundle pack writes a strict
archive from current valid content without changing the directory workspace.
Unreferenced local files are not portable bundle members.

sections.heading: SSMD bundle workspaces
sections.text:
SSMDConvert stores converted books and single documents in one kind-neutral
artifact lifecycle. The manifest identifies whether a bundle contains a book or
a document; users do not choose a storage type.
sections.lower:
ssmdconvert stores converted books and single documents in one kind-neutral
artifact lifecycle. the manifest identifies whether a bundle contains a book or
a document; users do not choose a storage type.

sections.heading: Canonical names
sections.text:
An editable workspace is a directory named <name>.ssmd-bundle/. A portable,
immutable archive is named <name>.ssmd-bundle.zip. Both contain the existing
kind-specific manifest format and schema version; the outer artifact name is
shared.

novel.ssmd-bundle/
novel.ssmd-bundle.zip
notes.ssmd-bundle/
notes.ssmd-bundle.zip

sections.heading: Convert and inspect
sections.text:
ssmdconvert bundle inspect novel.epub --json
ssmdconvert bundle convert novel.epub --chapters 2-20 -o novel.ssmd-bundle
ssmdconvert bundle convert notes.md -o notes.ssmd-bundle
ssmdconvert bundle convert reviewed.ssmd.md
ssmdconvert bundle validate novel.ssmd-bundle




When the output is omitted, conversion creates a directory workspace beside the
source using its filename stem. --force replaces the complete existing
workspace atomically. bundle inspect accepts a supported source or a canonical
bundle and reports the detected kind.

--chapters selects original, one-based source chapter numbers for books. A
single document accepts the default all value; another chapter selector is a
usage error. Book chapters remain in source order.

sections.heading: Lifecycle commands
sections.text:
The bundle command group contains exactly these lifecycle operations:


inspect SOURCE inspects a supported source or bundle.


convert SOURCE creates an editable workspace.


metadata BUNDLE displays stored metadata.


refresh WORKSPACE updates recorded content digests; --check only checks
whether the workspace is clean.


pack WORKSPACE creates a deterministic .ssmd-bundle.zip archive.


validate BUNDLE strictly checks the manifest and referenced content.



Only a directory workspace can be refreshed or packed. ZIP archives are
read-only. validate and strict bundle loading verify manifest hashes; analysis
workflows can read current valid content from a dirty directory workspace
without silently refreshing it. Packing reads current valid workspace content
and does not change the workspa…

sections.heading: Document manifest format (implementation detail)
sections.text:
This page documents the existing single-document manifest carried inside a
canonical bundle. It is an implementation detail; users manage either source
kind through the common lifecycle described in Bundle workspaces.

The document manifest keeps its existing format identifier and schema version:

format:         ssmdconvert.document
schema_version: 1
ssmd_version:   0.9




The manifest contains JSON-compatible metadata, source provenance, and one
canonical document entry with ID document-0001, path document.ssmd.md,
character count, and content digest. Manifest JSON is UTF-8 and strict JSON;
metadata must be JSON-compatible. The source digest is captured during
conversion, and publication does not reread the source.

the source workspace. Unreferenced local files are not portable members.

sections.heading: ssmdconvert speech audit
sections.text:
Audit automatic speech-preparation changes without modifying SSMD.

ssmdconvert speech audit SOURCE
ssmdconvert speech audit BOOK.ssmd-bundle.zip --chapters 3 --json
ssmdconvert speech audit SOURCE --language en-US --fail-on-warning




Audit uses the same source loader, selected chapters, generic change IDs, and
analysis pipeline as report; it is a speech-focused view, not a separate
normalizer. --json emits a versioned JSON result. --fail-on-warning returns a
non-zero status when the audit contains warnings or errors. --language, chapter
selection, fallback mode, and title inclusion control the analysis as in report.

sections.heading: ssmdconvert txt
sections.text:
Project SSMD into generic prepared plain text for downstream TTS tools. The
projection uses the same selected sections and rendering logic as the report’s
TXT preview and statistics.

ssmdconvert txt SOURCE
ssmdconvert txt BOOK.ssmd-bundle.zip --chapters 2-8 -o prepared.txt
ssmdconvert txt SOURCE --language de-DE --no-include-titles




Text goes to stdout by default. -o writes a file atomically; an existing output
requires --force, and the input cannot be used as the output. --chapters,
--language, --sequence-fallback-mode, --max-paragraph-chars, and title
options have the same meaning as in report. TXT is a projection only: it does
not contain SSMD source annotations and does not write back to the source.

sections.heading: Python API
sections.text:
from ssmdconvert import AnalysisOptions, TextProjectionOptions, analyze_ssmd, project_text

analysis = analyze_ssmd("chapter.ssmd", options=AnalysisOptions(spacy="off"))
projection = project_text(
    analysis,
    options=TextProjectionOptions(max_paragraph_chars=1000, include_titles=True),
)
prepared_text = projection.text
output_digest = projection.stats.prepared_output_sha256




Pass the same projection to build_report(analysis, projection=projection) to
keep report statistics and the prepared-output digest tied to the exact TXT
returned to the caller. No file is written by project_text().

See Report and SSMD analysis workflows.

sections.heading: CLI usage
sections.text:
SSMDConvert uses one bundle lifecycle for EPUB books, ordinary documents, and
existing SSMD sources. Every editable workspace ends in .ssmd-bundle; a packed
archive ends in .ssmd-bundle.zip.
sections.lower:
ssmdconvert uses one bundle lifecycle for epub books, ordinary documents, and
existing ssmd sources. every editable workspace ends in .ssmd-bundle; a packed
archive ends in .ssmd-bundle.zip.

sections.heading: Convert, inspect, and validate
sections.text:
ssmdconvert bundle inspect novel.epub --json
ssmdconvert bundle convert novel.epub --chapters 2-20 -o novel.ssmd-bundle
ssmdconvert bundle convert notes.md -o notes.ssmd-bundle
ssmdconvert bundle convert reviewed.ssmd.md
ssmdconvert bundle validate novel.ssmd-bundle




When -o is omitted, bundle convert creates an editable workspace beside the
source. Existing outputs are refused unless --force is supplied; forced
workspace publication replaces the complete directory atomically.

--chapters accepts original one-based book chapter numbers, as a number, a
range, a comma-separated list, or a mixture such as 1,3-5. It defaults to
all. A non-default selector is not valid for a single-document source.

sections.heading: Standalone SSMD conversion
sections.text:
The top-level converter remains available for writing one standalone SSMD file:

ssmdconvert convert manuscript.txt -o manuscript.ssmd
ssmdconvert convert report.pdf -o report.ssmd
ssmdconvert inspect manuscript.md --json




PDF and DOCX inputs require the matching optional extras. Writes are atomic and
refuse existing outputs unless --force is supplied. The input file is never a
valid output destination.

Conversion commands accept --metadata-file PATH for a UTF-8 YAML mapping.
Metadata precedence is source, file, and explicit CLI values. The sequence
fallback mode defaults to preserve; the option is available when a caller
needs spell.

language: de-DE
voice_defaults:
  narrator:
    rate: slow

Analysis accepts standalone SSMD and canonical directory or ZIP bundles.
Speech audit is read-only. Annotation and freeze publish a new destination and
never modify a workspace in place. See analysis and speech workflows
for cache freshness, language behavior, and output policy.
